items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Terminology 32:1
items.html: No degree can ascend and be corrected except to its upper one, which is close to its level. For example, AVI cannot ascend to Atik, but only to AA; and all that is corrected in Atik is AA. And likewise all that is corrected in AVI is YESHSUT, and all that is corrected in YESHSUT is ZON. And the reason for the matter is that all the corrections of the lower one in its upper one are because the AHP of the upper one are always attached to the GAR of the lower one, and therefore the GAR of the lower one ascends with the upper one at the time when the upper one raises its AHP, as is known. Thus, at the time when the upper one sorts and raises its AHP from the Klipot, the GAR of its lower one is also found ascending and being sorted with it. And likewise in the attainment of Mochin: for example, the AHP of AA are found in his HGT, and at the time when AA returns the Mochin, to lower the bottom Hey from his openings of the eyes and to raise the AHP to the discernment of his GAR, then these AHP raise with them also his HGT to the discernment of his head, because they are attached one to the other. And then AVI also ascend with the HGT to the head of AA, since they are the garments upon the HGT of AA. And in this manner is the order of the ascents of all the Partzufim, as is known. Thus, only the lower one adjacent to him has the power to ascend to the upper one — either by reason of its being attached to the AHP of the upper one, or by reason of its clothing the HGT of the upper one. But this does not apply at all to the degree beneath his lower one. (Item 22).
